description: Privy session-signer policy for the Volatus hedger agent. Maps README.md's abstract policy (allow streamPremium|adjustCoverage on SigmaStream only, deny all other ERC-20 transfers, cap cumulative spend at the mandate) onto SigmaStream's real deployed ABI and selectors on Arc Testnet.

chain.name: Arc Testnet
chain.note: Gas on Arc is USDC itself (BRIEF.md) — this policy governs which contract calls the session signer may make, not gas sponsorship, which is a separate Privy/Circle concern out of scope here.

rules.name: streamPremium
rules.description: subscribe() and fund() move the delegator's own USDC into a stream they already authorized, from their own wallet, into subscription.funded for an epoch they chose. Never a transfer to a third party.

methods.name: subscribe
methods.abi: subscribe(uint256 epochId, uint256 ratePerSecond, uint256 coverageNotional)

rules.name: adjustCoverage
rules.description: Re-prices a live subscription's rate and notional. adjust() runs _sync() first (contracts/src/SigmaStream.sol), so every second already elapsed bills at the OLD rate before the new one takes effect — re-rating can never retroactively re-price coverage already accrued. This is the seam the hedger agent drives (BACKEND_HANDOFF.md § Service 3).

methods.name: adjust
methods.abi: adjust(uint256 epochId, uint256 newRatePerSecond, uint256 newCoverageNotional)

rules.name: approveStreamSpend
rules.description: USDC.approve with spender constrained to SigmaStream only. Without this rule fund() reverts on the ERC-20 allowance check before it ever reaches the contract's own logic — easy to miss, called out explicitly in BACKEND_HANDOFF.md and PHASES.md.

rules.name: denyEverythingElse
rules.description: Default-deny. This is an allowlist: any ERC-20 transfer/transferFrom, any approve to a spender other than SigmaStream, any call to a contract other than SigmaStream or USDC, is denied. Rules above are the entire allowed surface.

spendCap.description: Cumulative USDC moved via fund() across the life of one mandate. Enforced two ways, deliberately redundant: Privy's TEE is asked to enforce this numeric cap against this policyId, and this service independently re-derives cumulative spend from its own journal before ever attempting a fund() (services/hedger/src/spend.ts) and refuses to exceed it regardless of what Privy would allow. Neither is a substitute for the other — the TEE bound holds even if this service's code is wrong or compromised; the journal-side check holds even if a specific Privy policy instance was misconfigured.
spendCap.note: A concrete numeric limit is set per mandate at policy-instantiation time (one Privy policy grant per user session, scoped to one mandate), not hardcoded in this file.

expiry.description: The session signer's grant should be set to expire no later than Mandate.expiresAt. An expired mandate that Privy still honors would be a provisioning bug, not something this policy file can fix from the agent side — the agent's own code also stops attempting any action once Mandate.expiresAt has passed (mandate.ts's mandateExpired), independent of what Privy would still allow.

verificationNote: Selectors were computed and confirmed against the deployed SigmaStream ABI with `cast sig` (see services/hedger/src/delegation/signer.test.ts, which asserts the same selectors from encoded calldata). PRIVY_APP_ID and PRIVY_APP_SECRET were not available in this environment (BACKEND_HANDOFF.md's environment table lists them unset), so this policy has never been submitted to Privy's policy API or exercised by a real TEE. src/delegation/privySessionSigner.ts is unit-tested against a mocked client only — see that file's header comment for exactly what is and is not verified.
